plan.title: bug(plan-sequence): batching_allowed is persisted but never authorizes parallel entries

narratives.Description: The ordered plan stores `batching_allowed: true`, but `verify:plan-sequence` and `swarm:launch` admit only the single current entry, so an approved parallel wave runs one entry at a time. Launch admission also checks a dummy `story:swarm-cohort` target against the stored cursor instead of the real roster against the derived cursor (#6205). This story gives entries a `batch` label, admits every pending entry of the current batch when `batching_allowed` is true, keeps single-entry behavior when it is false, and makes launch check its real roster.
narratives.UserStory: As an operator who approved a parallel wave in the ordered plan, I want every pending entry of the current batch admitted at push and launch time, so that the wave runs in parallel without dropping the plan file, while later batches stay refused.
narratives.ImplementationPlan: 1. `packages/core/src/plan-sequence/types.ts`: optional entry `batch` label (closed shape, parse, create); `planBatchError` refuses `batching_allowed: true` with no labels or a split label at set time; legacy unlabeled files read as one entry per batch. 2. `packages/core/src/plan-sequence/derive.ts`: `derivePlanBatch` returns the pending, unfinished entries of the current batch from the derived cursor. 3. `verifyPlanTarget` admits any entry of that set; new `verifyPlanStory` matches a launch roster member (story id, or resolved issue set) against the same set. 4. `packages/core/src/swarm/launch.ts`: `admitSwarmLaunchPlanSequence` passes terminal origins and checks each real roster member, solo included; while a plan file is present the consent token is not an admission path; with no file the #1378 token rule is unchanged. 5. `plan-sequence:current` prints the authorized set; `plan-sequence:set` refuses bad batch labels. 6. Docs in `content/commands.md`, one CHANGELOG line, core and CLI tests.
narratives.Traces: #4433; operator ruling comment 6906744991; accepted synthesis 6179223813 (Bound lean 6179017430); #6205; #2402; #1378; #4129
narratives.Constraint: Operator ruling 6906744991 amends the Bound lean: `batching_allowed` is honored, not rejected; entries the plan marks as one batch are admitted together. Where a clause says 'current entry' or 'reject', the item Acceptance narrative states the amended behavior. No second batch store; the label lives on the plan entries.
narratives.Overview:
- Dispatch-time cohort consent: Allocation context / classifyAllocation token presence. classifyAllocation does not see target T and does not own a wave set. explicitConsent is dest T-admission only when no sequence is active. Dest CLI skip does not read the token; dest skip is dest permit when the file is absent.
- Serial current-entry T-admission: dest-placed verifyPlanTarget on entries[current_index], plus #4129 on that one entry when terminalOrigins are passed. Observed at this pin: admitSwarmLaunchPlanSequence uses dummy target swarm-cohort and does not pass terminalOrigins. That dummy-target match is not a harvest requirement and MUST NOT stand in for roster verification.
- Precedence by sequence state. Active sequence (file present; exhausted counts as active): plan-sequence owns admission, serially, for every swarm:launch roster, including solo. Input is the real resolved roster, not dummy story:swarm-cohort. Each roster member must be the current entry. verifyPlanTarget remains the owner. Named and unnamed launches share this refuse. No active sequence (file absent): the #1378 token owns cohort admission; dest-placed CLI verify:plan-sequence skips permit-and-proceed; complete-cohort-sweep multi-story named launch with no sequence stays allowed.
- Exhausted sequence (file present, verifyPlanTarget exhausted): the sequence is active. Do not treat exhausted as absent. Singleton named launch is refused as exhausted.
- Match key: a story-kind entry matches on story_id. An issue-kind entry matches when the entry's id or issue is in the story's resolved issues set. A story that maps to several issues matches if the resolved issue set is exactly the current entry's identity.
- Sequence file reach: dest-placed predicate 2 runs only when .deft/plan-sequence.json is present in that checkout. Consumers MAY commit it. Launch may read the primary working-tree file while a dest reads the copy committed on its base branch; after advancePlanSequence without a commit those copies can disagree. Record that split in the harvest; do not invent a shared store.
- Reject batching_allowed: true at set/parse; document the pointer to the consent token as dispatch-time token presence, not dest T-admission while a sequence is active; rewrite the AC list so a reject PR can close. On the reject branch, decide the read path for already-persisted batching_allowed: true files.
- Restate severity as a misleading state contract plus serialized throughput, not a security hole. Do not add a second batch store. Do not teach dest pre-PR to accept the minted #1378 token as a substitute for current-entry T-admission while a sequence is active.

## Refutation verdict: the target survives

Quoting the recorded Stop 1 field:

> plan-sequence accepts and reports batching_allowed: true, but verifyPlanTarget and resolveContinuation only authorize entries[current_index], so an approved parallel peer is indistinguishable from a later wave.

Re-verified by running the anchors against the pinned source, not by reading line cites. Repro built from `packages/core/src/plan-sequence/types.ts` at dispatch-sha, three entries A/B/C, `batching_allowed: true`:

```
batching_allowed persisted: true
batching_allowed round-trip: true
verify A: {"ok":true,"entry":{"id":"A",...},"index":0}
verify B: {"ok":false,"code":"mismatch","message":"Target issue:B is not the current ordered-plan entry (issue:A)."}
verify C: {"ok":false,"code":"mismatch","message":"Target issue:C is not the current ordered-plan entry (issue:A)."}
resolveContinuation("next"): {"action":"advance","entry":{"id":"A",...},"index":0}
after advance: index 1 statuses A:completed,B:pending,C:pending
```

B and C are byte-identical denials. `git grep batching_allowed` at dispatch-sha returns exactly five non-test sites: `types.ts:36` (field), `types.ts:225`/`:238` (create), `types.ts:309` (parse), `cli/plan-sequence.ts:102` (set). Zero read sites. `PlanSequenceEntry` (`types.ts:23-29`) carries no grouping field. `advancePlanSequence` (`types.ts:248-267`) mutates only `entries[current_index]` and a scalar. The premise is confirmed at the repo revision, not only in the 0.116.0 dist the body cites.

The refutation charter therefore has nothing to attack in the premise. Everything below attacks what the issue concludes from it.

## blocks-the-design - the acceptance criteria pre-decide the "Required design decision"

**Evidence.** The body says "Choose and document one deterministic model" and AC 1 is a genuine disjunction: executable semantics **or** rejected as unsupported. But AC 2 ("schema deterministically identifies the authorized current batch/frontier"), AC 3 (`verifyPlanTarget` accepts every pending entry in the current batch), AC 5 (out-of-order peer completion), AC 6 (advance only when every batch entry is terminal) and AC 10 (guidance no longer says only "Current sequence entry" *when a batch is active*) are satisfiable only on the schema-change branch. Regression tests 1, 2, 3 and 6 likewise presume batches exist. AC 7 (`batching_allowed: false` preserves single-entry behavior) is vacuous on the reject branch.

**Failure mode.** An implementer takes the cheap branch the body explicitly permits - reject `batching_allowed: true` at set/parse, roughly the `types.ts:238`/`:309` pair plus `cli/plan-sequence.ts:102` - ships a correct fail-closed fix, and still leaves five unchecked boxes. The `content/skills/deft-directive-pre-pr/SKILL.md` closing-keyword policy allows `Closes #N` only when the full issue DoD is met, so that PR must either false-close or carry a schema migration nobody chose. In practice the checklist, not the design decision, picks the expensive branch.

**Disposition consequence.** The lean cannot bind as written. The successor lean has to name one branch, and if it names reject-or-defer it must rewrite the AC list in the same move rather than inheriting it.

## blocks-the-design - Directive already has an executable batch-authorization mechanism, and it is not in plan-sequence

**Evidence (inventory before proposing a new mechanism).** `content/templates/agent-prompt-preamble.md:30-50` defines `## Allocation context` with `dispatch_kind: solo | swarm-cohort`, `allocation_plan_id`, `batching_rationale`, and a recognition contract. `content/skills/deft-directive-swarm/references/core-phase-0.md:52` states it plainly: "That token IS the batched approval for the whole cohort." This is not prose-only - `classifyAllocation` in `packages/core/src/story-ready/evaluate.ts` fails closed with exit 1 on `swarm-cohort` plus a null `allocation_plan_id` or `batching_rationale`, and `packages/core/src/session/posture.ts:106` parses `dispatch_kind`. Directive therefore already ships one batch-authorization surface with a deterministic evaluator.

**Failure mode.** The reported incident is two surfaces disagreeing, not one surface missing. A worker dispatched for issue 515 under an approved cohort passes the Story Start Gate (cohort consent satisfied) and fails `verify:plan-sequence` (not `entries[current_index]`). Adding batch fields to `plan-sequence.json` creates a *second* store answering "who is in the current wave," with independent write paths and no reconciliation. The body names #3913 (authority census) as "not a duplicate" - but two batch surfaces is exactly the input a census exists to reconcile, and nothing in the proposed ACs reconciles them. Post-fix, a cohort of three with `allocation_plan_id` set and a hand-written plan-sequence batch of two can both be "valid" and disagree, which is the failure the Impact section already fears ("throughput and the ordered plan can disagree while both appear valid") reproduced one layer up.

## Summary

`plan-sequence` accepts, persists, parses, and reports `batching_allowed: true`, but no runtime behavior reads the field when resolving or verifying an authorized target. `verify:plan-sequence` always permits only `entries[current_index]`, so a user-approved parallel batch is silently enforced as a serial plan.

This is a fail-closed authorization defect with a misleading state contract: the stored plan says batching is allowed, but the only creation/dispatch gate rejects every peer except the first entry.

## Observed version

- `@deftai/directive@0.116.0`
- `@deftai/directive-core@0.116.0`
- macOS / zsh / Node 24.18.0

The behavior was first observed in a consumer delivery session whose ordered plan placed issues 512 and 515 in the same explicitly named parallel wave with `batching_allowed: true`. Issue 512 passed the gate; issue 515 could not pass until the sequence advanced. The second implementation was checkpointed and paused, then required a later recovery/delivery cycle.

## Minimal reproduction

```sh
repro_root=$(mktemp -d)

deft plan-sequence:set \
  --project-root "$repro_root" \
  --from-json '{
    "sequence_id": "parallel-wave-repro",
    "sequence_kind": "cohort",
    "entries": [
      {"id": "A", "kind": "issue", "title": "Parallel wave A / first"},
      {"id": "B", "kind": "issue", "title": "Parallel wave A / second"},
      {"id": "C", "kind": "issue", "title": "Next serial wave"}
    ],
    "authorized_by": "operator-approved repro",
    "batching_allowed": true,
    "continuation_past_final": false
  }'

deft plan-sequence:current --project-root "$repro_root" --json

deft verify:plan-sequence \
  --project-root "$repro_root" \
  --target-kind issue \
  --target A \
  --json
echo "$?"

deft verify:plan-sequence \
  --project-root "$repro_root" \
  --target-kind issue \
  --target B \
  --json
echo "$?"
```

Observed results:

```text
OK plan-sequence set parallel-wave-repro (3 entries, index=0)

"batching_allowed": true

{"ok":true,"entry":{"id":"A",...},"index":0}
0

{
  "ok": false,
  "code": "mismatch",
  "message": "Target issue:B is not the current ordered-plan entry (issue:A)."
}
1
```

Entry C also fails, which is correct while wave A is active. The defect is that B is indistinguishable from C even though B is an approved peer in the current parallel wave.

## Expected behavior

Directive should have one explicit, deterministic contract:

1. If `batching_allowed` is supported, the data model must identify exact batch boundaries, and all current-batch entries must pass target verification while later batches remain denied.
2. Completing one peer out of order must not advance beyond unfinished peers in the current batch.
3. `plan-sequence:current` must report the complete currently authorized set, not imply that only one entry is authorized.
4. If batch boundaries cannot be represented, `plan-sequence:set` must reject `batching_allowed: true` instead of persisting a no-op authorization field.

`batching_allowed: true` must never widen authorization to every later plan entry. The narrow ordered-plan invariant from #2402 still applies.

## Actual behavior and implementation evidence

The installed 0.116.0 artifacts show that the field is a write/read-only decoration:

- `dist/plan-sequence.js` forwards `raw.batching_allowed === true` into `createPlanSequence`.
- `@deftai/directive-core/dist/plan-sequence/types.js:139-155` stores it.
- `types.js:173-218` parses and preserves it.
- `types.js:64-98` (`resolveContinuation`) selects only `entries[current_index]` and never reads `batching_allowed`.
- `types.js:99-138` (`verifyPlanTarget`) compares only `entries[current_index]` and never reads `batching_allowed`.
- `types.js:157-171` (`advancePlanSequence`) marks only the current entry completed and increments a scalar index. It cannot represent an out-of-order peer completion or wait for the rest of a batch.
- The public `PlanSequenceEntry` type has no `batch_id`, wave index, dependency set, or equivalent grouping field. A single plan-level boolean therefore cannot distinguish B (same wave) from C (later wave).

The CLI and docs also describe “Current sequence entry only,” so the implementation is internally serial even when the persisted contract advertises batching.

## Impact

- Explicit operator-approved parallel work is serialized.
- Agents can correctly read `batching_allowed: true` yet still be denied when dispatching the second worker.
- The mismatch encourages agents to pause valid work, seek unnecessary renewed approval, or hand-edit/advance the plan prematurely.
- Premature advance would be worse: it can mark the first entry completed before its product/lifecycle work is actually complete and can authorize a later wave while a peer remains unfinished.
- Swarm/cohort throughput and the ordered plan can disagree while both appear valid.

## Required design decision

The current schema cannot express which entries share a batch. Choose and document one deterministic model, for example:

- nested ordered batches, each containing one or more entries; or
- an explicit `batch_id` / `wave` on each entry plus a current batch cursor; or
- a dependency/readiness model from which the current authorized frontier is derived.

Do not infer batches from title text such as “Parallel wave A.” Do not interpret the plan-level boolean as “all remaining entries may run concurrently” unless that broad authorization is explicitly intended and migration-safe.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] `batching_allowed` has executable semantics or is rejected as unsupported; it is not accepted as a no-op field.
- [ ] The schema deterministically identifies the authorized current batch/frontier.
- [ ] `verifyPlanTarget` accepts every pending entry in the current batch and rejects entries in later batches.
- [ ] `resolveContinuation` and `plan-sequence:current` expose the same current authorized set as the verifier.
- [ ] Completion can target a specific entry, including out-of-order peer completion, without falsely completing another peer.
- [ ] The sequence advances to the next batch only when every required entry in the current batch is terminal under the defined policy.
- [ ] `batching_allowed: false` preserves current single-entry behavior.
- [ ] Exhaustion remains fail-closed and explicit queue/backlog overrides keep the #2402 boundary.
- [ ] Invalid or ambiguous batch metadata fails closed with one actionable remediation.
- [ ] Generated consumer guidance no longer says only “Current sequence entry” when a batch is active.

## Regression tests

Add core and CLI coverage for at least:

1. Batch A contains A1 and A2; batch B contains B1. A1 and A2 pass; B1 fails.
2. A2 completes first. A1 remains authorized; B1 remains denied.
3. A1 completes. Only then does B1 become current and pass.
4. `batching_allowed: false` authorizes only the scalar current entry.
5. A malformed or missing batch boundary with `batching_allowed: true` fails closed at `set`/parse time.
6. Text and JSON output from `plan-sequence:current` enumerate the same authorized set enforced by `verify:plan-sequence`.
7. Existing single-entry and sequence-exhaustion tests remain green.

## Related issues; not duplicates

- #2402 introduced the ordered-plan boundary and explicitly requested a “whether batching is allowed” field. It is closed, and its delivered field currently has no executable batching semantics.
- #3910 covers merge-order safety across multiple lifecycle artifacts, not current-batch target authorization.
- #3913 covers authority census/reconciliation, not parallel target selection.
- #4129 detects a scalar current entry whose lifecycle entity is already terminal, not multiple concurrently authorized entries.

## Scope note

This issue is about the ordered-plan runtime contract and its CLI/core tests. It does not request weakening the fail-closed plan boundary, bypassing target verification, or changing unrelated swarm readiness/file-overlap policy.
